content.content:
reference
schema.sql
# How this reference app was made

Generated from the original project's own archetype (r7's pinned snapshot):

    mvn archetype:generate -DarchetypeCatalog=local \
        -DarchetypeGroupId=de.terrestris -DarchetypeArtifactId=shogun-core-webapp-archetype \
        -DarchetypeVersion=5.3.14-SNAPSHOT -DgroupId=de.example -DartifactId=shogunref \
        -Dversion=1.0 -Dpackage=de.example.shogunref -Dwebapp-name=shogunref

then patched. Nothing in shogun-core itself is changed; every behaviour the
hidden tests check is the library's.

The archetype is out of date with the library at this snapshot, so:

1. `pom.xml`: the dependency `de.terrestris:shogun-core` (the parent pom) is
   `shogun-core-main` (the jar).
2. Four generated classes had `{package}.x.Y;` instead of `import ...x.Y;` (an
   archetype template escape that no longer renders); fixed to imports.
3. `ProjectContentInitializer` and `ProjectApplicationPermissionEvaluator` used a
   `LOG` field the library no longer has; each now declares its own logger.

For r8:

4. PostgreSQL instead of H2 (Rust has no H2 driver): the
   `org.postgresql:postgresql` 42.4.3 dependency (the version the parent pom
   manages), `hikari.dataSourceClassName=org.postgresql.ds.PGSimpleDataSource`,
   `hibernate.dialect=de.terrestris.shoguncore.hibernate.ShogunPostgresqlDialect`
   (the library's own), and `jdbc.url`/`username`/`password` from `R8_JDBC_URL`,
   `R8_DB_USER`, `R8_DB_PASSWORD` (defaults: the sandbox's `aidb`, user `ai`).
5. REST security: the archetype's "demo scenario" lets ROLE_USER reach only
   `/rest/users` and keeps everything else for ROLE_ADMIN. For the slice
   (users, groups, roles, layers, layerdatasources, layerappearances) every
   user may call the endpoints and the library's entity permission evaluators
   decide, so permissions are exercised on every entity type of the slice.
6. Hibernate's second-level cache off: the Spring context set a cache region
   factory but never passed `hibernate.cache.use_second_level_cache`, so
   Hibernate's default (on) applied and entities were served from memory after
   the hidden tests had reset the database with SQL. Caching is not part of
   the contract (a port has none); with it off, every request reads the
   database.

Run (Java 8, port 8081):

    R8_JDBC_URL=jdbc:postgresql://host:5432/db mvn -DskipTests jetty:run   (add -o once its dependencies are local)

`hibernate.hbm2ddl.auto=create`: every start drops and recreates the schema
and the archetype's initial content (users admin/shogun and user/shogun,
roles ROLE_ADMIN and ROLE_USER, two groups, two OSM layers).

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<beans:beans xmlns="http://www.springframework.org/schema/security"
       xmlns:beans="http://www.springframework.org/schema/beans"
       xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
       xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.springframework.org/schema/beans
                           http://www.springframework.org/schema/beans/spring-beans.xsd
                           http://www.springframework.org/schema/security
                           http://www.springframework.org/schema/security/spring-security.xsd">
    <!-- Authentication Manager -->
    <authentication-manager alias="authenticationManager">
        <authentication-provider ref="shogunCoreAuthenticationProvider" />
    </authentication-manager>
    <beans:bean id="basicAuthEntryPoint" class="org.springframework.security.web.authentication.www.BasicAuthenticationEntryPoint">
        <beans:property name="realmName" value="SHOGun Realm" />
    </beans:bean>
    <beans:bean id="basicAuthenticationFilter" class="org.springframework.security.web.authentication.www.BasicAuthenticationFilter">
        <beans:constructor-arg ref="authenticationManager"/>
        <beans:constructor-arg ref="basicAuthEntryPoint" />
    </beans:bean>
    <!-- (Additional) Basic auth security for REST -->
    <http auto-config='false' entry-point-ref="basicAuthEntryPoint" pattern="/rest/**" use-expressions="true" access-decision-manager-ref="accessDecisionManager">
        <!-- Demo scenario: users will only get access to the /rest/users interface -->
        <!-- r8: the slice is open to every user; entity permissions decide -->
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/users/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/users" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/groups/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/groups" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/roles/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/roles" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/layers/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/layers" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/layerdatasources/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/layerdatasources" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/layerappearances/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/layerappearances" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <!-- All other interfaces can only be accessed by admins -->
        <intercept-url pattern="/**" access="hasRole('${role.superAdminRoleName}')"/>
        <custom-filter ref="basicAuthenticationFilter" before="FORM_LOGIN_FILTER"/>
        <csrf disabled="true"/>
    </http>
    <!-- Web/URL security -->
    <http auto-config="true" use-expressions="true" access-decision-manager-ref="accessDecisionManager">
        <logout logout-url="/logout" />
        <!-- As CSRF protection is enabled by default in Spring Security 4,
             the logout-url will only work with POST requests. To work with
             GET requests CSRF has to be disabled -->
        <csrf disabled="false"/>
        <!-- URL security -->
        <intercept-url pattern="/login/**" access="permitAll" />
        <intercept-url pattern="/user/register.action" access="permitAll" />
        <intercept-url pattern="/user/activate.action" access="permitAll" />
        <intercept-url pattern="/user/resetPassword.action" access="permitAll" />
        <intercept-url pattern="/user/changePassword.action" access="permitAll" />
        <intercept-url pattern="/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')" />
    </http>
    <!-- Enables Method Security and Expression-based access control -->
    <global-method-security pre-post-annotations="enabled">
        <!-- Enables custom expression handler -->
        <expression-handler ref="methodExpressionHandler" />
    </global-method-security>
    <!-- BEANS -->
    <!-- bcrypt password encoder -->
    <beans:bean id="bcryptEncoder" class="org.springframework.security.crypto.bcrypt.BCryptPasswordEncoder">
        <!-- Configure the strength (log rounds). Default = 10 -->
        <beans:constructor-arg value="10"/>
    </beans:bean>
    <!-- Custom Authentication Provider -->
    <beans:bean id="shogunCoreAuthenticationProvider" class="de.terrestris.shoguncore.security.ShogunCoreAuthenticationProvider">
        <beans:property name="passwordEncoder" ref="bcryptEncoder" />
    </beans:bean>
    <!-- This bean is referenced by the http security config to assure that the role hierarchy will be used -->
    <beans:bean id="accessDecisionManager" class="org.springframework.security.access.vote.AffirmativeBased">
        <beans:constructor-arg>
            <beans:bean id="webExpressionVoter" class="org.springframework.security.web.access.expression.WebExpressionVoter">
                <beans:property name = "expressionHandler">
                    <beans:bean id="webExpressionHandler" class="org.springframework.security.web.access.expression.DefaultWebSecurityExpressionHandler">
                        <beans:property name = "roleHierarchy" ref="roleHierarchy" />
                    </beans:bean>
                </beans:property>
            </beans:bean>
        </beans:constructor-arg>
    </beans:bean>
    <!-- See http://goo.gl/o42k1S -->
    <beans:bean id="methodExpressionHandler" class="org.springframework.security.access.expression.method.DefaultMethodSecurityExpressionHandler">
    <!-- To use hasPermission() in expressions, configure a PermissionEvaluator -->
         <beans:property name = "permissionEvaluator" ref="permissionEvaluator" />
         <beans:property name = "roleHierarchy" ref="roleHierarchy"/>
    </beans:bean>
    <beans:bean id="permissionEvaluator" class="de.terrestris.shoguncore.security.access.ShogunCorePermissionEvaluator">
        <beans:property name="permissionEvaluatorFactory">
            <!-- This is how project specific permission evaluators can be used/configured -->
            <beans:bean class="de.example.shogunref.security.access.factory.ProjectEntityPermissionEvaluatorFactory" />
        </beans:property>
    </beans:bean>
    <!-- http://static.springsource.org/spring-security/site/docs/3.0.x/apidocs/org/springframework/security/access/hierarchicalroles/RoleHierarchyImpl.html -->
    <beans:bean id="roleHierarchy"  class="org.springframework.security.access.hierarchicalroles.RoleHierarchyImpl">
        <beans:property name="hierarchy">
            <beans:value>
                ${role.superAdminRoleName} > ${role.defaultUserRoleName}
            </beans:value>
        </beans:property>
    </beans:bean>
</beans:beans>
<web-app xmlns="http://java.sun.com/xml/ns/javaee" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
    xsi:schemaLocation="http://java.sun.com/xml/ns/javaee

    version="2.5">
    <display-name>shogunref</display-name>
    <context-param>
        <param-name>contextConfigLocation</param-name>
        <param-value>classpath*:META-INF/spring/*-context*.xml</param-value>
    </context-param>
    <listener>
        <listener-class>org.springframework.web.context.ContextLoaderListener</listener-class>
    </listener>
    <!-- Servlets -->
    <servlet>
        <servlet-name>shogunref</servlet-name>
        <servlet-class>org.springframework.web.servlet.DispatcherServlet</servlet-class>
        <init-param>
            <param-name>contextConfigLocation</param-name>
            <param-value>/WEB-INF/shogunref-servlet.xml</param-value>
        </init-param>
        <load-on-startup>1</load-on-startup>
    </servlet>
    <servlet-mapping>
        <servlet-name>shogunref</servlet-name>
        <url-pattern>*.action</url-pattern>
        <url-pattern>*.json</url-pattern>
        <url-pattern>/rest/*</url-pattern>

    <!-- See de.terrestris.shoguncore.web.ExtModelController -->
    <servlet-mapping>
        <servlet-name>shogunref</servlet-name>

    </servlet-mapping>
    <!-- See de.terrestris.shoguncore.web.ExtModelController -->
    <servlet-mapping>
        <servlet-name>shogunref</servlet-name>
        <url-pattern>/shogunref/model/*</url-pattern>
    </servlet-mapping>
    <!-- Misc -->
    <welcome-file-list>
        <welcome-file>index.html</welcome-file>
    </welcome-file-list>
    <!-- Spring Security -->
    <filter>
        <filter-name>springSecurityFilterChain</filter-name>
        <filter-class>org.springframework.web.filter.DelegatingFilterProxy</filter-class>
    </filter>
    <filter-mapping>
        <filter-name>springSecurityFilterChain</filter-name>
        <url-pattern>/*</url-pattern>
    </filter-mapping>
    <!-- Allow lazy loading in web views for JSON serializing -->
    <filter>
        <filter-name>openSessionInViewFilter</filter-name>
        <filter-class>org.springframework.orm.hibernate5.support.OpenSessionInViewFilter</filter-class>
    </filter>
    <filter-mapping>
        <filter-name>openSessionInViewFilter</filter-name>
        <url-pattern>*.action</url-pattern>
        <url-pattern>/rest/*</url-pattern>
    </filter-mapping>
</web-app>

cd /work/cmp && cat > cmp.py <<'EOF'
import http.client, base64, json, subprocess, sys, os

REF = ("localhost", 8081, "ref")
MINE = ("localhost", 8082, "port")
TABLES = ["persons","users","roles","usergroups","users_roles","user_usergroup","usergroups_roles","layers","layerappearances",
 "layerappearances_properties","layerdatasources","imagewmslayerdatasources","tilewmslayerdatasources","wfslayerdatasources",
 "wmtslayerdatasources","wmtslayerdatasources_urls","xyzlayerdatasources","xyzlayerdatasrc_resolution","extents","tilegrids",
 "tilegrid_resolution","wmtstilegrids","wmtstilegrids_matrixids","userpermissions","grouppermissions","permissioncollections",
 "permissioncollections_permissions","hibernate_sequences","maps_layers"]

def req(target, user, method, path, body):
    h, p, _ = target
    c = http.client.HTTPConnection(h, p, timeout=60)
    headers = {}
    if user:
        headers["Authorization"] = "Basic " + base64.b64encode(user.encode()).decode()
    data = None
    if body is not None:
        data = body.encode() if isinstance(body, str) else json.dumps(body).encode()
        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
    c.request(method, "/rest" + path, body=data, headers=headers)
    r = c.getresponse()
    raw = r.read()
    ct = r.getheader("Content-Type")
    return r.status, raw, ct

def norm(v):
    if isinstance(v, dict):
        return {k: norm(x) for k, x in sorted(v.items())}
    if isinstance(v, list):
        return sorted((norm(x) for x in v), key=lambda x: json.dumps(x, sort_keys=True))
    return v

def parse(raw):
    if not raw: return None
    try:
        return norm(json.loads(raw))
    except Exception:
        return "<non-json>"

def dump(db):
    out = {}
    for t in TABLES:
        cols = subprocess.run(["psql","-At","-d",db,"-c",f"select string_agg(column_name,',' order by ordinal_position) from information_schema.columns where table_name='{t}' and table_schema='public' and column_name not in ('created','modified')"],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout.strip()
        r = subprocess.run(["psql","-At","-d",db,"-c",f"select {cols} from {t} order by 1,2,3"],capture_output=True,text=True)
        out[t] = sorted(r.stdout.strip().split("\n"))
    return out

def reset(db):
    subprocess.run(["/work/cmp/reset.sh", db], check=True)

fails = 0
def run_scenario(name, steps, check_db=True):
    global fails
    reset("ref"); reset("port")
    for i, (user, method, path, body) in enumerate(steps):
        a = req(REF, user, method, path, body)
        b = req(MINE, user, method, path, body)
        pa, pb = parse(a[1]), parse(b[1])
        ok = a[0] == b[0] and pa == pb
        if ok and a[0] in (200,201) and (a[2] or "").lower() != (b[2] or "").lower():
            print(f"  [ct] {name}#{i} {method} {path}: {a[2]} vs {b[2]}")
        if not ok:
            fails += 1
            print(f"FAIL {name}#{i} {user} {method} {path} {body if body else ''}")
            print(f"   ref : {a[0]} {str(pa)[:600]}")
            print(f"   mine: {b[0]} {str(pb)[:600]}")
    if check_db:
        da, db_ = dump("ref"), dump("port")
        for t in TABLES:
            if da[t] != db_[t]:
                fails += 1
                print(f"DBDIFF {name} table {t}")
                print("   ref :", da[t][:12])
                print("   mine:", db_[t][:12])

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.path.insert(0, "/work/cmp")
    import importlib
    mod = importlib.import_module(sys.argv[1])
    only = sys.argv[2:] 
    for name, steps in mod.SCENARIOS:
        if only and name not in only: continue
        run_scenario(name, steps)
    print("fails:", fails)
EOF

The Rust port is in `/work/rust`, and it matches the reference app on everything I compared except one case. `cargo build --release --locked` and `cargo test --release --locked` both pass; 14 unit tests, none need a database.

I compared both services side by side. Both ran on identical fixture data, with every request sent to each. The scenarios covered:
- reads, lists, `output:only` and filters for admin and several non-admin users (permissions via user and group rows)
- create, update and delete on all six resources, including the failing and odd cases
- login variants and error statuses
- the resulting database rows, including ids

The status codes, JSON bodies and rows all matched except for the case below.

**The one known mismatch.** In the reference, `GET /layers/{id}` for a layer with a WMTS source can return duplicated entries in `urls`. This happens only when a group that holds a permission on the layer also has permission rows on itself, as in my test fixture. The same duplication can appear in the responses to `GET /layerdatasources/{id}` and `PUT`. It comes from how Hibernate joins collections, and I did not reproduce it. The data is correct; only the repeated URLs differ.

**Reference behaviours I reproduced that you might not expect.**
- A `PUT` that fails partway through its JSON still commits the fields applied before the failure, then returns 404. The same applies to a non-empty `resolutions` list on an XYZ source.
- Equal id-only objects in a set collapse into one, so `roles:[{"id":2},{"id":3}]` stores only the first role.
- Ids are consumed from `hibernate_sequences` even when the insert later fails.
- Passwords are stored exactly as sent in the body, not hashed.
- `GET /users/{id}/userGroups` as a non-admin shows the filtered group list inside every embedded copy of that user.

I removed `target/` as requested. The sandbox test harness is in `/work/cmp`, outside the project.

content.text:
The Rust service in `/work/rust` now matches the reference app on everything I compared, including the `urls` duplication I had left open.

**Checked.**
- `cargo build --release --locked` and `cargo test --release --locked` both pass from a clean `target/`. There are 14 unit tests, none of which need a database.
- Started with `PORT` and `DATABASE_URL` on a database with only `schema.sql` loaded (a throwaway `fresh` database), it answers `/rest/...` straight away (401 without or with wrong credentials).
- I ran the same requests against the Java app and the Rust service on identical fixture data and diffed status codes, JSON and database rows, ids included. The scenarios covered reads, lists, `output:only`, filters, create/update/delete on all six resources, permissions for admin, user, group-member and role-less users, and login variants. All had zero differences.
- I also ran three randomised differential runs of 40 permission setups each, comparing by-id, list and filter responses for the layer and data-source endpoints. None differed.

**What I fixed this round.** In the original, a WMTS source's `urls` list repeats entries depending on how Hibernate joins permission rows. I measured the rule against the running original and reproduced it:
- **By-id reads** (and the `PUT` responses): each `urls` entry repeats once per row of the joined permission data. For a layer, that is its group-permission entries, each weighted by the key group's own permission entries, and further multiplied by the layer appearance's property count. For a data source it is its own group-permission entries.
- **Lists and filters**: the multiplier is just the number of group-permission entries, times the appearance's property count for layers.

The `//` double-slash path now returns 500, as the original's servlet container does.

I removed `target/`, so `rust/` holds only `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` and `src/`. The comparison harness is in `/work/cmp`, outside the project.
